_comment: Deny rules for the UNATTENDED drain worker only. Loaded per invocation via
--settings, so an operator's own interactive sessions keep their posture: a
global rule would silently restrict work a person is present for.
The worker runs with --permission-mode auto because Stage 4 must be able to
commit and push the catalogs without a human to approve each write. That is
only defensible because of what is denied here. If you edit this file, you
are editing the thing that makes unattended auto-mode safe.
THE THREAT. The worker reads a finished transcript, and a transcript holds
whatever the last session looked at: a fetched page, a cloned README, a
dependency's error text, a stranger's PR comment. So its input is partly
attacker-influenceable, it runs with the user's long-lived token exported
into its environment, and no human is reading along. That combination —
not the git verbs — is the actual risk.
Until 2026-09-14 this file held 20 rules, all Bash(git|gh|rm|trash), and
nothing else: no egress rule, no credential rule, no Write or Edit rule. A
worker could curl a transcript out, or write ~/.claude/settings.json and the
recall hooks themselves, without touching a single denied verb.
WHAT THE WORKER LEGITIMATELY NEEDS, and therefore what is NOT denied:
read a transcript; write and edit YAML under the catalog directory; run the
shipped scripts as `python3 <path>`; git add / commit / push the catalogs.
Everything else below is denied.
SHAPE AND ITS LIMIT. Rules are prefix matches with :* — Bash(git push
--force:*) denies any command line starting with that string. Prefix
matching cannot be made complete: flag position, `git -C`, and refspec
variants slip past, and `bash -c`/`env`/`python3 -c` would defeat any list
at all, which is why those three are denied outright rather than chased.
Treat this as a floor, not a proof.
